prompt: A Voltmarkt report adds each order line's promotion name and must keep every line, those with no promotion included (order_lines.promo_id is missing for them). Check the join for the orders placed from 7 to 20 April 2025 (the UTC days of order_ts). Return three columns, in this order: lines_before (the order lines of those orders), rows_after (the rows once each line has its promotion's name, missing where it had none) and added_rows (rows_after minus lines_before). Return one row. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row for the whole check

hints: Next, write the comparison of the two row counts.
Take the count before the join away from the count after it: 0 means the join kept one row per line.
faded_shape:
WITH period_lines AS (
  -- one row per order line of an order placed from 7 to 20 April 2025 (UTC days of order_ts)
  SELECT l.order_line_id, l.promo_id
  FROM order_lines l
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
  WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-07 00:00:00'
    AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-21 00:00:00'
), with_promo AS (
  -- one row per order line, with its promotion's name (missing when the line had none)
  SELECT w.order_line_id, p.promo_name
  FROM period_lines w
  LEFT JOIN promotions p ON p.promo_id = w.promo_id
), counts AS (
  -- one row: the row count before and after the join
  SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM period_lines) AS lines_before,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM with_promo) AS rows_after
)
SELECT lines_before, rows_after,
why_this_works: A LEFT JOIN on the line's own promo_id finds at most one promotion per line and keeps the lines without one, so no row is added or lost.
